$comment: What flowapi holds itself to: against the other generators (speed), and building whole SDK repositories (sdk-repo). `cargo run --release --bin check` reads the results a rule names (`results`, results/speed.json when none) and fails on any rule a run breaks. A ratio is the best other tool's figure over flowapi's on each description; `except` lowers it for one description, where the measurement says less. Change a number only together with its reason, in the change that moves it.

rules.about: flowapi's output type-checks on every description, with tsc --strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
flowapi, the whole process timed, is at least 10x faster than the fastest other generator on every description.
flowapi's peak resident memory is no more than the leanest other generator's on every description.
Every repository's config, an example's or one drafted, passes `config check` with no error and no warning.
The judge's verdict is pass on every repository, every step of 0-6 run and passed.
`generate`, the whole process into an empty folder, takes at most this many milliseconds (median) on the repositories named; each must be measured.

why.cloudflare: One run by hand on 2026-11-26 (Intel N150, 4 cores): 16.3 s, 217 MB, 1,237 files for Cloudflare's 3,935 operations, on a drafted config. 30 s leaves room for a slower machine and the noise of a laptop, and fails a change that doubles the time. Lower it from the first full run's median.

rules.about: On every live agent run kept (bench/agent/run.sh), the judge, run by the runner after the agent, passes steps 0-6. The runs are the owner's: paid and not deterministic, so their absence is said and does not fail, and their turns, cost and time hold to no budget.
